treeHeightCeiling.title: How tall can a tree get?
treeHeightCeiling.turgorNote: How well the topmost leaves can still fill with water and grow.
treeHeightCeiling.failNote: Past the ceiling the water column snaps — the top can no longer drink.
treeHeightCeiling.verdictOk: The crown is still paying its way: water reaches the top under survivable tension.
treeHeightCeiling.verdictOver: Beyond what the plumbing allows here. On Earth this is impossible; on Pandora, lower gravity and a CO2-rich, humid atmosphere lift the ceiling — straining toward Hometree's scale, not sailing past it.
treeHeightCeiling.hint: A tree has no pump: it drinks by pulling an unbroken thread of water up its wood, powered only by evaporation from its leaves. The taller it grows, the harder the top must pull, until the leaf cells can no longer fill — Koch & Sillett (2004) put Earth's ceiling near 130 m. Switch to Pandora and watch lower gravity and dense, carbon-rich air move that ceiling.

shannonChannel.title: Shannon's channel, made playable
shannonChannel.subtitle: C = B · log₂(1 + S/N)
shannonChannel.aria: Channel capacity {capacity}; the chosen payload takes {time} to cross.
shannonChannel.hint: Drag bandwidth and watch the answer move in great linear strides; drag the signal-to-noise ratio and watch it barely budge. Bandwidth is the precious resource — raw power is almost useless. Then send a whole connectome down the biological cable and see why an overnight transfer of a mind is impossible the maximalist way, and merely extravagant the minimalist way.

consciousBottleneck.title: The conscious bottleneck
consciousBottleneck.subtitle: Eleven million bits in; a few dozen bits of self out
consciousBottleneck.compressionNote: sensation thrown away per bit kept
consciousBottleneck.aria: The senses pour in eleven million bits per second; only {conscious} reaches awareness — a {compression}-fold compression.
consciousBottleneck.hint: Your senses pour ~11 Mb/s into the nervous system, yet the stream that reaches awareness — the self that thinks and remembers — runs at a mere handful of bits per second. Slide that rate and watch a whole lifetime of selfhood collapse to mere tens of gigabits: small enough, at last, to send across the bond in a single night.

squareCube.title: The square-cube law
squareCube.hint: Double an animal's length and its mass goes up eightfold, but the bone cross-section that carries it goes up only fourfold. The stress on every bone therefore doubles. That is why a body cannot simply be scaled up - its shape is forced to change.

froudeDial.title: Froude gait dial
froudeDial.hint: At the same leg length, Pandora's lower gravity pulls every gait transition down to a lower speed. The pa'li breaks into its efficient spring-loaded gaits sooner - and each footfall lands softer for it.

flightCeiling.title: The wall every flyer hits
flightCeiling.hint: The demand curve climbs steeper than the supply curve, so they always cross. The crossing is the heaviest a flyer can still flap. Pandora's lower gravity and denser air pull the demand curve down - sliding the crossing rightward, to a mass Earth would pin to the ground.

wingspanLadder.title: A ladder of fliers
wingspanLadder.subtitle: Wingspan, drawn to one scale
wingspanLadder.hint: Earth's largest fliers top out near 11 m - Quetzalcoatlus marks the wall, and everything to the right of the dashed line is airspace Earth's physics forbids. The rideable ikran sits right on that wall; the toruk leaves the chart, at roughly double the largest creature Earth ever flew.

reynoldsRegime.title: What kind of air?
reynoldsRegime.subtitle: Re = ρ·v·L / μ
reynoldsRegime.hint: The Reynolds number measures whether the air behaves like sticky syrup (low Re - the insect's rowing world) or a thin clean stream a sleek wing can slice (high Re - birds, pterosaurs, banshees). It rises with size, speed, and air density - so Pandora's denser air nudges a flier of any given size up into the friendlier, cleaner regime.

superconductor.title: Superconductor cool-down
superconductor.hint: Drop the temperature below Tc: resistance falls straight to zero and the magnet locks, hanging in mid-air.
